Fresh maintained/adoption evidence through 2026-07-28 strengthens the hypothesis that an explicit composer-local contract is more defensible than header-first or generic global inference: a maintained extension records a ChatGPT header model control moving into a composer pill after redesign and later composer input-width regressions, while independent selector configs retain explicit editor/Send/upload/voice anchors. Project-local README/task prompt still contain former review-after-round freeze wording. Canonical Personal-Forge Policy B and current state govern execution until DOCS-RECONCILIATION repairs that drift.

Primary DOM/HTML standards evidence supports using an ordinary in-flow span/div with one open ShadowRoot and external Ghost mount manager as the provisional first shell-host primitive rather than an autonomous custom element. This removes custom-element registry/callback lifecycle state but does not authorize any current ChatGPT insertion slot. Repair must revalidate generation/current container before DOM writes, coalesce ResizeObserver-driven repair, bind Shadow controls directly to reviewed Ghost handlers, and fail closed to the rail.

The eventual structural shell must remain host-flow-first across virtual-keyboard models. VisualViewport resize may schedule bounded verification but may not become x/y/bottom placement authority; Ghost must not edit viewport interactive-widget policy or opt the host into VirtualKeyboard overlay behavior. Because VirtualKeyboard is limited-availability, it is optional-only. Certification should include 320-CSS-pixel-equivalent reflow, 200% text scaling, visual-only and layout-resize keyboard models, orientation, listener cleanup/coalescing, and separate Android WebView claim discipline.

Future structural-shell performance stress should separate deterministic hosted evidence from physical-device claims. Use Playwright Chromium CDP at 1x/4x/6x CPU slowdown with invariant-based correctness/resource gates and descriptive median/p95 timing only; CPU throttling is relative to the host and cannot certify mobile CPU architecture. Firefox remains a separate correctness lane because Playwright CDP is Chromium-only. Physical Android/AVD/WebView/GeckoView remain separate evidence surfaces.

Existing reviewed input/Send profiles are not structural-mount authorization. Future structural capability must fail closed when absent, reuse shared invariant/repair machinery, and keep adapter-owned discovery/insertion rules. Anchor-smoke selector health is lower evidence than authenticated structural capture, which is lower than mount certification. No non-ChatGPT adapter inherits ChatGPT's insertion rule by analogy.

A future structural Shadow host must add no new Trusted Types HTML sink. ShadowRoot.innerHTML remains TT-governed; current Ghost already proves that a restrictive trusted-types allow-list can block gitl-ui and drive existing HTML sinks to fail loud. Prefer a DOM-built in-flow host/Shadow subtree, preserve the named-policy boundary, keep MV3 structural mounting viable in the default isolated content-script world, and do not require MAIN-world/unsafeWindow authority. Browser TT support is broad in 2026, but host CSP enforcement remains site-specific and is not inferred for every adapter.

verificationSummary.repairConstraints: Generation/current-container revalidation before writes; one scoped MutationObserver and one ResizeObserver owned by the mount manager; ResizeObserver callbacks schedule/coalesce rather than synchronously resize; Shadow controls bind directly to reviewed Ghost handlers; any verification failure removes only Ghost-owned structure and restores the rail.
verificationSummary.mobileReflowConstraints: Treat VisualViewport/keyboard geometry as verification input, not placement authority; support visual-only and layout-resize keyboard models; never change host viewport/VirtualKeyboard policy; VirtualKeyboard optional-only; gate at 320-CSS-pixel-equivalent reflow and 200% text; coalesce resize/orientation verification; fail closed when Blue/Red crowding or clearance cannot be proven.
verificationSummary.constrainedRuntimeConstraints: Tier A: Chromium-only Playwright CDP at CPU rates 1x/4x/6x, identical structural/safety assertions, stable mount/observer/listener/pending-repair counts, zero Send-adjacent actuation, clean throttle/session teardown, and descriptive timing only. Tier B: separate physical Android/AVD evidence when a device claim is required. Do not promote Pixel emulation or hosted CPU throttle to physical-device certification; do not attach CDP throttle claims to Firefox.
verificationSummary.crossAdapterConstraints: Reviewed actuation/input profiles do not grant structural mutation authority. Use three evidence stages: anchor smoke (no mutation authority), adapter-specific authenticated structural capture, then mount certification. Shared code may own invariant checks/repair/teardown, but each adapter owns structural discovery and approved insertion rules. Missing structural capability means rail-only. ChatGPT remains first proof target; Claude/Copilot are provisional next capture priorities only; Manus needs fresh structural corroboration; DeepSeek/Gemini need stronger re-review; Perplexity/Grok remain higher-ambiguity; matched-but-unreviewed hosts stay rail-only.
verificationSummary.compatibilityConstraints: Future structural shell must add no new Trusted Types HTML sink. Do not render the Shadow interior through shadowRoot.innerHTML by default; prefer DOM-built nodes and direct handlers, preserve the existing named-policy boundary, avoid a permissive default policy, keep extension mounting viable in isolated content-script world, and do not require unsafeWindow/MAIN-world authority. Add deterministic no-actuation compatibility cases for ordinary CSP, TT enforcement with gitl-ui allowed, policy-name rejection, limited ShadowRoot.setHTML availability, and extension-isolated execution. Existing whole-product blocked-policy behavior remains fail-loud and is not reclassified as a current PASS.
verificationSummary.platformClaimLimits: Chrome Android viewport behavior does not certify WebView. Physical Android, Android WebView, Firefox-Android/GeckoView, real IME combinations, and calibrated low-end-device performance remain separately uncertified.
